title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity as companies pivot towards satellite technology and defense budgets are being recalibrated. Meanwhile, the specter of funding challenges looms large over ambitious projects.

themes.title: Satellite Imagery Innovations
themes.body: BlackSky's Lyn Chassagne emphasizes the role of satellite imagery in problem-solving, highlighting a growing trend among companies to leverage data for actionable insights. This shift could redefine how businesses and governments approach decision-making in a data-driven world.

themes.title: Capital Raises and New Ventures
themes.body: Creotech's $118 million capital raise for a new satellite factory signals a robust interest in expanding satellite manufacturing capabilities. Similarly, Cowboy's $275 million funding to develop rockets with orbital data centers underscores the increasing appetite for innovative space solutions.

themes.title: Defense Budget Dynamics
themes.body: The failure to pass a defense budget is being viewed as a self-inflicted wound in the space race, potentially stalling critical projects. However, the recent $1.4 billion addition to the space resilience line in the FY27 budget markup suggests that some funding priorities are being reassessed.

themes.title: Collaborative Defense Initiatives
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid reflects a trend of collaboration among defense contractors to enhance space capabilities. This partnership could set a precedent for future joint ventures aimed at bolstering national security in the orbital arena.
